name: Improving Horizontal Well Delivery Through Real-Time Drilling Alignment and Faster Field Decision-Making
author: Lin
description: We were addressing costly non-productive time and delayed field decisions during horizontal drilling operations, and this win aligned with the organization’s broader goals of improving operational efficiency, protecting project margins, increasing client confidence, and delivering wells more safely and predictably.

answers.winName: Improving Horizontal Well Delivery Through Real-Time Drilling Alignment and Faster Field Decision-Making
strategy: We were addressing costly non-productive time and delayed field decisions during horizontal drilling operations, and this win aligned with the organization’s broader goals of improving operational efficiency, protecting project margins, increasing client confidence, and delivering wells more safely and predictably.

This win positioned the organization as a more reliable and operationally disciplined drilling partner by reducing downtime, improving decision speed, increasing well delivery consistency, and demonstrating the ability to execute complex horizontal drilling projects more efficiently than competitors.

The team analyzed recurring NPT trends, approval delays, directional drilling pauses, and communication bottlenecks from previous wells and discovered that faster alignment between the rig crew, directional drillers, geosteering specialists, and supervisors could significantly reduce downtime and improve horizontal well delivery performance.
workPlan: We implemented a WITSML-enabled real-time drilling dashboard combined with trigger-based alignment huddles, allowing the rig crew, directional drillers, geosteering specialists, and supervisors to review the same live well data together and make faster field decisions that reduced downtime and kept the horizontal section on plan.

The dashboard and alignment huddles streamlined the horizontal well delivery process by giving every stakeholder access to the same live drilling data at the same time, allowing issues to be identified earlier, decisions to be made faster, and corrective actions to happen before delays escalated into costly downtime or target-window deviations.

The most critical dependency was the hand-off between the directional drilling team and the geosteering specialists during live formation changes, and it was managed through real-time alignment huddles, shared dashboard visibility, and predefined escalation triggers that ensured decisions were made quickly before drilling delays or target-window deviations occurred.
people: The Directional Drilling Coordinator drove adoption of the real-time dashboard by demonstrating how faster alignment reduced downtime, leading daily alignment huddles, training crews on live data usage, and building trust with the rig team by showing that the system improved decisions instead of adding operational complexity.

The Directional Drilling Coordinator drove adoption of the WITSML-enabled dashboard by addressing rig team concerns about extra complexity, data overload, and unclear decision ownership, then making the tool relatable through short field examples, simple trigger points, and live demonstrations showing how shared data could reduce downtime and make their work easier.

The Directional Drilling Coordinator was the most critical stakeholder because they translated the dashboard’s technical drilling data into simple field-ready trigger points, trained the rig team using real examples, and kept the process focused on faster decisions, less downtime, and practical support for the crew instead of adding complexity.
operations: The win was supported by the WITSML-enabled real-time drilling dashboard, MWD/LWD telemetry, geosteering updates, trigger-based alignment huddles, shift handoff routines, escalation protocols, and clear ACT decision ownership policies, all of which improved horizontal well delivery by helping teams identify issues earlier, align faster, reduce downtime, and keep drilling operations on target.

The integration streamlined horizontal well delivery by ensuring every shift started with the same live drilling context, predefined escalation paths, and shared operational priorities, allowing the rig crew, directional drillers, and geosteering specialists to respond to issues faster, maintain alignment across teams, and reduce delays caused by miscommunication or incomplete handoffs.

The dashboard and trigger-based huddles improved shift handoffs by giving each incoming crew the same live drilling context, current risks, target-window status, and agreed next actions, which overcame incomplete handoff notes, repeated explanations, unclear ownership, and decision delays that could have caused downtime or well path deviations.
results: The most significant reduction was cutting non-productive time from about 9.5 hours on comparable wells to 3.2 hours on this well, which improved drilling efficiency by keeping the horizontal section moving with fewer delays and protected profitability by reducing rig standby costs and avoiding expensive corrective work.

We tracked total NPT hours, rig standby time, decision turnaround time, alignment huddle response time, number of unplanned drilling pauses, course-correction delay time, target-window accuracy, shift handoff completeness, repeated clarification requests, and percentage of field decisions made using shared dashboard data.

The project reduced non-productive time from 9.5 hours to 3.2 hours on comparable wells, improved target-window drilling accuracy, shortened field decision turnaround times, reduced unplanned drilling pauses, improved shift handoff consistency, and delivered the horizontal section ahead of schedule with fewer corrective actions and lower operational cost.
